items.markingKey: (d) It is incorrect. It multiplies each element by 2; a list would be repeated.

Dev is learning how to create NumPy arrays:
import numpy as np
a = np.arange(4, 29, 4)
b = np.linspace(0, 3, 4)
c = np.zeros((2, 3), dtype=int)
print(a, a.size)
print(b)
print(c.shape, c.ndim)
(i) Write the output of the first print statement. (1)
(ii) Write the output of the second and third print statements. (1)
(iii) Give two differences between the list [1, 2, 3] and np.array([1, 2, 3]). (2)
items.answer: (i) [ 4  8 12 16 20 24 28] 7 (ii) [0. 1. 2. 3.] / (2, 3) 2 (iii) A list can hold elements of different types, an array holds one type; list * 2 repeats the list, array * 2 multiplies each element (arrays support element-wise arithmetic and use less memory)
